text:
Let the direction in the \(x\)-\(z\) plane be parameterized by the polar angle \(\theta\):

\[
\vec n=(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta).
\]

The spin operator along \(\vec n\) is

\[
P_{\vec n}=\vec P\cdot\vec n
=\frac{\hbar}{2}
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\
\sin\theta & -\cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Solving

\[
P_{\vec n}\,\chi_+=\frac{\hbar}{2}\chi_+
\]

gives the normalized spinor

\[
\chi_+=
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos(\theta/2)\\[2pt]
\sin(\theta/2)
\end{pmatrix},
\]

since \(\cos^2(\theta/2)+\sin^2(\theta/2)=1\). An arbitrary overall phase is physically irrelevant.

Answer: B
